messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall - potential degraded API reachability observed for redwood-hosted endpoints. Alert: high 5xx from edge and TLS handshake failures. Please ack.
Olivia: acked. jumping on it. what regions are we seeing this from?
Emma: I'm seeing spike in 524/525 and a lot of TLS timeouts from EU/NA edge, traces show lots of `tls: handshake failure` in our ingress logs.
Raj: seeing DNS lookup failures for some Cloudflare hostnames, and a few origins returning 502. Running `dig +short A api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` shows intermittent nil responses.
Ben: Cloudflare status page is showing a problem in a few PoPs, link: https://cloudflarestatus.com/incidents (looks partial). CloudflareStatusBot: New incident reported: "Edge TLS handshakes degraded in select POPs" - https://cloudflarestatus.com/edge-tls
Marta: Support already getting customer messages — ticket #7892 flagged: "API errors since ~09:12 UTC". Impact: some customers seeing failures on embed and chat routes.
Olivia: oncall plan: 1) confirm scope 2) mitigation 3) communicate. Emma/Raj can you confirm if our failover routing to alternate region is healthy?
Emma: prefix cache/KV is fine. The service layer can route to us-east-1 or eu-west-1; but the problem looks at the CDN layer before it hits origin. Our origin logs show healthy responses when we hit them directly.
Raj: running quick curl direct to origin IP bypassing Cloudflare: `curl -vk --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:34.120.200.11 https://api.redwood.example.com/health` -> returns 200 and TLS OK (so origin is fine).
Ben: can we short-circuit Cloudflare for affected customers? We have a contingency to set a DNS ALIAS to origin LB for select customer IPs but DNS TTLs may bite us.
Olivia: trigger Cloudflare fallback policy? Any way to force traffic to another provider?
Emma: Cloudflare has a config to disable HTTP/2/0-RTT in the affected POPs but that's their side. I've opened a ticket with Cloudflare support and linked our logs. CloudflareStatusBot: Support ticket #CF-112233 created, awaiting response.
Raj: temp mitigation: add an ip-based route in our edge routers to prefer direct path when `tls: handshake failure` observed and marked customer cohorts to use origin via a special header. Doing a canary for 5% of traffic to direct-origin path now.
Olivia: roll the canary. Marta, please draft a short status for customers: explain degraded reachability, mitigation in progress, ETA TBD. Keep it generic re: provider.
Marta: Draft: "We are investigating intermittent API errors and TLS handshakes affecting some requests. We have activated a targeted fallback and will update shortly. If you see persistent errors, please reply with example request IDs." Thoughts?
Ben: good. Also add that embedding/regen endpoints are affected. No PII.
Emma: telemetry: enabling additional debug logs for edge TLS handshake failures. Pushing a config that captures SNI and cipher details for failures.
Olivia: Pager handoff: I'm on for next 30m then Emma takes over. @pagerduty-bot make note.
pagerduty-bot: Olivia acknowledged. Next oncall: Emma in 30m.
Raj: Observed pattern: certain SNI chains result in `alert handshake_failure` from Cloudflare side; other SNI values pass. Could be upstream cert negotiation or middlebox. Running `openssl s_client -connect <edge>:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -tls1_3` shows failures on some POPs.
Emma: trying to change our origin TLS profile to temporarily accept older ciphers (enable TLS1.2 fallback). Doing it in canary first.
Ben: committing routing rule to route 20% of traffic from affected countries to direct-origin bypass. Deploying in 2m.
Marta: Customer comms updated: "We've activated a targeted fallback routing for affected requests and are monitoring. We will post updates every 30 minutes." Posting to status.redwood.ai
Olivia: Cloudflare replied: "We're investigating an SNI mismatch issue in several POPs; we've pushed mitigation to some edges. Please continue your canaries and report any improvements."
Emma: After the bypass rollout, error rate in canary fell from 8% -> 0.5% for those requests. Looks promising.
Raj: note: because TTLs are high for some domains, DNS-based fixes are slow; our edge-router header-based routing is faster.
Olivia: escalation: if Cloudflare mitigation doesn't stabilize in 45m, we'll open plan B (full customer routing to alternative CDN / direct origin with short TTL).
Ben: Plan B prep: we have Fastly config & keys ready; prepping a quick re-route runbook. Will need to notify sales/enterprise customers before cutover.
Marta: I've queued a targeted message to affected customers and enterprise AE list. Waiting on final approval.
Emma: continued monitoring: adding traces for tokenized request IDs so we can correlate failing clients to CDN PoPs.
Olivia: thank you team. Emma taking lead. I'll update #oncall-handoff in 30m. For now, status page updated and customers notified.
CloudflareStatusBot: Update: "Mitigation deployed to additional PoPs; customers may see intermittent improvements. Investigation continues."
Olivia: initial incident note: impact: partial API reachability degradation, increased TLS handshake failures across Cloudflare POPs, customer-facing 5xx errors on chat/embed routes. Mitigation: targeted direct-origin fallback for affected traffic, Cloudflare mitigation in progress. Owner: Olivia -> Emma.
Marta: Support: adding affected customers to priority queue, capturing request IDs.
Raj: saving collected dig/openssl logs to /var/logs/incidents/1953000000_tls.csv and uploading to incident ticket.
Emma: I'll keep the thread updated every 15m or on any status change.
Olivia: handoff complete. continuing to monitor. :white_check_mark:
